key_insight: This paper tests whether a strong teacher’s token-by-token feedback helps a smaller model reach a target accuracy with less training compute than reinforcement learning. The provided abstract is truncated, so it does not establish which approach wins or under what conditions.
problem_solved: Determine whether on-policy distillation’s dense supervision translates into real compute savings over Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), rather than simply faster progress per training step.
method: Compare vanilla reverse-KL on-policy distillation, using student-generated rollouts and a frozen teacher’s per-token supervision, against GRPO.
Vary task difficulty, student and teacher sizes, domains, and optimization choices.
Measure held-out accuracy against training FLOPs to assess compute efficiency.
impact: The comparison can help practitioners evaluate whether teacher-guided distillation or reinforcement learning better fits a limited training budget. Specific recommendations require the paper’s full results.
visual_elements: Side-by-side training diagrams: student rollouts with frozen-teacher feedback versus GRPO updates.
